title: Dynamics of Erased Distinctions
summary: A living synthesis of the project’s current view of coarse-graining: closure tracks which distinctions remain causally relevant, how erased distinctions return to visibility, and when representation repair must restore them.
thesis: Groovy Commutator studies the dynamics of distinctions erased by a representation.

title: Dimensional Closure and the Commutator Lift
summary: The dimensional program now separates several representation-relative resources rather than treating added coordinates as dimension by fiat. The zero-dimensional selector audit exposes mandatory role overlap; relational rank distinguishes available translation directions from law-used causal directions but adds no classifier for the accepted axial constructor; and the finite interface-history audit shows that one or two lags of the existing touching-strip interface coordinate still fail every frozen local-closure budget. These exact bounded results leave intrinsic dimension, alternative coordinates, deeper history and stronger autonomous organization open.
thesis: When two dynamical paths fail to commute, represent the disagreement as a new coordinate and ask whether the enlarged representation closes.

title: Invariants Across Representation Contracts
summary: Eleven audits complete across four transformation types: global relabelings, an injective local recoding, linear and non-linear observations, and a change of wiring. Reflection and coprime whole-contract dilation preserve every exact property audited, with the seeded sweep labels only stable; complement conjugation and dilation are exactly covariant only when the companion object, the derivative or the observation, is transported with the rule; closure under an observation and its history cost are properties of the pair and are genuinely changed. A twelfth audit, factor locality on observation images, is accepted: idempotent observations bound the factor radius by construction, and the one whole-ring factor coincides with the one ring-dependent closure. A thirteenth audit certifies closure at every ring size from a sixteen-vertex pair graph: six audited observations stabilize from ring 7, and the two linear observations that alternate are certified to alternate forever. A fourteenth audit certifies refinement depth at most one at every ring from a 256-vertex pair graph per rule and finds that, unlike closure, depth on the full shift is not decided by the periodic configurations under four observations. The fifteenth audit decides full-shift depth at most two for every rule by sparse reachability, finds the same gap at depth two under seven observations, and shows that twenty-four rules with depth at most one on every ring have depth at least three on the full shift. The Program page carries the verdict matrix and what each other program can use.
thesis: Which properties of a represented dynamics survive a declared change of representation contract, after transporting what must be transported, and at what cost?
